correctness.rationale: The explicit channel has nonnegative entries and sends rare-start transitions to common-start transitions for every correlation. Tensorization and signed stochastic contraction give the exact norm reduction; weighted transpose symmetry from detailed balance provides L1/Linfinity equality for complex as well as real parameter combinations. The derivative formula is the coefficient of (z-1)^k in the binomial generating-function derivative. Its k=1 first-difference total variation is twice the peak binomial mass. The Gaussian-Hermite limit is a CLT plus score generating-function second moment k!(n)_k/[q(1-q)]^k, guaranteeing uniform integrability. The critical Poisson limit follows from total variation convergence of Bin(n-1,lambda/n). The finite checker passed 1698 exact rational comparisons and does not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: Pisier (2007) proves holomorphic semigroup factorization, Keller (2010) proves biased Boolean hypercontractivity, and O-Donnell (2014) states standard resampling noise operators. Their inspected statements do not imply a parameter-independent garbling from one rare-start row to every other transition row, nor the all-order exact operator-derivative norms and interior/critical limits. The earlier first-chaos rare-vertex norm covers only the special rho=0,k=1 case and is excluded from claims of novelty. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches revealed related, materially narrower objects; residual unindexed priority risk remains. Full texts of the two most similar published degree-two Fourier projection records were subsequently inspected and found to concern only fixed degree-two projectors, not semigroup derivatives.
residual_risks: The two closest published degree-two projection articles were inspected in full and cover fixed primitive idempotents, not the complete semigroup family; other unindexed spectral-projection literature could contain equivalent conclusions.
Historical literature on stochastic matrix garbling, product Markov-chain rows, and exact semigroup derivative total variation may be incompletely indexed.
The rho=0,k=1 first-chaos norm and some rho=0,k=2 uniform projection constants are already known specializations; they are explicitly not asserted as new.

value.rationale: Sharp endpoint derivative norms for finite biased noise semigroups quantify short-time semigroup regularity beyond classical hypercontractive estimates. A single parameter-independent channel controls all scalar spectral mixtures and all derivative orders, even with unequal coordinate probabilities; homogeneous cases yield an exact finite binomial law, fixed-order Hermite constants and a nontrivial n^1/2-to-n Poisson boundary transition. These are natural and reusable operator-theoretic invariants rather than isolated numerical examples.
